assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing chemically converts one base into another on genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, a clear mechanistic principle (engineered deaminase fused to a programmable nickase/dead Cas) that opened a new capability for precise genome chemistry. Impact is large and quickly generative, with clinical use emerging. It follows the 2020 CRISPR prize but is a distinct chemical invention, not a refinement of cutting.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual leader; Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors) were the lead trainee inventors of the two editor classes. Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work is credited but is a parallel, later or contemporaneous variant. A fair configuration is Liu alone or Liu with the two first-author inventors.
assessment.maturity: Eight to ten years of validation, many independent labs, therapeutic trials with reported patient benefit; timing is plausible, though close to the 2020 prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would split Liu from his trainees or recognise Liu alone, since only the listed names may be proposed.
Whether recognition is better combined with prime editing (B061) as one genome-editing chemistry citation.
Long-term clinical safety and off-target editing are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single DNA and RNA molecules electrically through an ionic current blockade, a clean physical principle that turned into a deployed, long-read sequencing technology with real-time and direct RNA capability. For a physicist this is attractive: quantitative single-molecule transduction that opened previously unforeseen applications.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brenner, Branton and Deamer demonstrated the concept in 1996; Bayley developed engineered protein pores and sensing chemistry; Akeson achieved processive enzyme-controlled DNA translocation. The credit is spread over several decades and contributors, and Branton's status is uncertain to me, so I propose three of the credited names who span concept, protein-pore engineering and sequencing realisation.
assessment.maturity: Commercial sequencing has been in wide use for about a decade with strong independent confirmation; recognition looks timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson is contested; I am uncertain about who is eligible.
Whether the committee views this as chemistry or as physics/medicine.
Next-generation sequencing prize overlap (2020s Sanger-style precedent) may complicate the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell reframes intracellular compartmentalisation in terms of physical chemistry (condensates, valency, weak multivalent interactions). It is a conceptually unifying, high-impact idea with a strong physical basis that connects to polymer physics.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed P granules behave as liquids in 2009; Rosen demonstrated multivalent phase separation of signaling proteins in 2012. Pappu and Mittag contributed theory and sequence grammar. The core trio seems the most defensible, but Pappu's theoretical role is a legitimate alternative.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly expanding field but with ongoing debate about physiological relevance, quantitative criteria for condensates, and how much in vitro droplets reflect in vivo behaviour; somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Controversy over how generally phase separation operates in living cells.
Whether this is chemistry rather than medicine or physics.
Attribution between cell-biology discovery and physical-chemistry framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale mass-spectrometry proteomics converted protein identification into a systematic measurement science (shotgun proteomics, isotope-coded and label-free quantitation, SWATH/DIA, deep proteomes). The analytical-chemistry impact on biology and medicine is very broad and well established.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution MS-based quantitative proteomics, SILAC), Aebersold (targeted and ICAT, SRM/DIA) and Yates (SEQUEST, MudPIT) have clearly distinct decisive contributions; Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also credited. Some risk because the 2002 prize already honoured Fenn and Tanaka for MS ionization.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely validated over three decades; recognition is more than timely and has been long anticipated.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 ionization prize may push the committee to want a narrower citation.
Choosing three among six credited names omits Hunt, Gygi and Heck.
Whether a single discovery can be identified, rather than a family of methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation re-purposes the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, a general principle that makes previously undruggable proteins targetable. It has a clear conceptual novelty and large generative potential, with many clinical programmes.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept in 2001; Ciulli provided structure-guided VHL ligands and degrader design; the glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray) links to thalidomide and cereblon. The credit is compound and one has to decide whether PROTACs and glues are a single discovery.
assessment.maturity: Clinical proof is still emerging, with several degraders in late-stage trials but no definitive approval of a PROTAC at the time I know; arguably early.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues form one prize or two discoveries with different credit.
Clinical efficacy is not yet established; I cannot verify current trial status.
Overlap with ubiquitin prize of 2004.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion uses orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs to site-specifically incorporate non-canonical amino acids, creating proteins with new chemistry in living cells. It is original, conceptually clean and very broadly used in protein engineering and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first orthogonal pair for a non-canonical amino acid in E. coli and eukaryotes with Wang; Chin extended to multiple codons, quadruplet decoding and animals, and genome recoding. Mehl and Yokoyama have further credited contributions.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of confirmation and wide adoption, though applications remain mostly in research and biologics rather than a transformative single outcome.
uncertainties: Impact per application is more diffuse than for a medical or industrial advance.
Allocation among Schultz, Wang and Chin is uncertain.
Close conceptual relation to the 2018 directed evolution prize and 2009 ribosome prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami folds a long scaffold strand with staples into arbitrary two- and three-dimensional nanostructures with nanometre addressability, an elegant principle of programmable self-assembly that connects to molecular machines, nanofabrication and biophysics, which resonates with the physicist's interest in designed molecular devices.
assessment.attribution: Seeman founded structural DNA nanotechnology but I believe he died in 2021 and he is not in the list; Rothemund invented origami in 2006; Yan and Yin extended it to 3D and single-stranded tile approaches, and Shih to 3D designs and functional devices. Winfree is credited for algorithmic assembly, a different branch.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation and thousands of designs, but applications such as drug delivery and computation remain at an early stage compared with the idea's elegance.
uncertainties: Real-world impact beyond research tools is limited so far.
Credit relative to Seeman's foundational role cannot be handled within this list.
Whether to cite the origami or the broader field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a rapid rise in solar-cell efficiency from about 4 to over 25 percent in a decade, with a physically rich story of long carrier diffusion lengths and defect tolerance. The generative potential for energy materials is large and the efficiency records are quantitatively striking.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell in 2009; Park and Snaith drove the solid-state and thin-film efficiency breakthroughs in 2012; Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis made further decisive contributions, so the allocation is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are unresolved, so the technology maturity is lower than the scientific maturity; the physics is well confirmed but the practical impact is not yet proven.
uncertainties: Long-term operational stability remains a major open problem.
Many credible claimants lead to a difficult three-person split.
Possible overlap with a physics prize rather than chemistry.
